channel.title: 522 PM
channel.description: 522 PM: what AI research found since the last episode, set in context: the papers worth the time and why, the technical developments from the labs, and the arguments, for technical people who are curious rather than researchers. Each episode is written and voiced by AI from public sources, which are listed under it. Brought to you by Lab522. Find us at https://www.lab522.co.uk. Email hello@lab522.co.uk.
channel.itunes:author: Lab522

item.title: What earns its keep, what counts as proof
item.description:
A controlled harness study asks which agent components justify their cost, while new environments test scientific coding and social reasoning. Plus, a challenge to Lean verification, faster video generation, selective thinking and a negative result for debate.

Sources:

item.title: Better scaffolding, unreliable stop signs
item.description:

item.title: Reasoning off the page, models off the disk
item.description:
A toy experiment shows how quickly a latent channel can defeat reasoning monitors, while an independent Astra replication finds more capability without visible working. New research cuts coding-agent traffic and streams expert models from disk; the AI safety debate reaches a much wider audience.

item.title: Copying apps, filtering traits, and checking the swarm
item.description:

item.title: Learning from routing, trading losses and hidden reasoning
